Harpak-ULMA launches hygienic robot loading with shared packaging controls

Washdown-oriented construction and Rockwell PLC motion control target simpler integration in food packaging lines.

Harpak-ULMA / Business Wire ↗1 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

A platform for food packaging

Harpak-ULMA introduced robotic loading for cheese, fresh meat and snacks on October 1. It locates, inspects, picks and loads products for thermoforming, flow wrapping and tray sealing. The company describes configurations reaching hundreds of packages per minute, depending on the product and layout, rather than guaranteeing that rate for every application.

Washdown and product handling

The food configuration uses open bent-plate stainless construction instead of tubular framing, with sloped drainage surfaces and accessible components. IP69K-rated components support demanding washdown. Application-specific tooling and 2D or 3D vision guide handling; product-presence, feature and defect inspection are selected according to the job.

A common maintenance environment

Robot motion is programmed directly in a Rockwell Automation PLC using Logix, shared with the packaging machines. Modular dimensions are configured during manufacture for the available space. Demonstrations are planned for PACK EXPO on October 18–21 and Automation Fair on November 16–19, 2026. Actual products and cleaning requirements still need application testing.
